*Grade a real run of a skill against the contract that skill committed to.*

> **Never assert what it did not observe.** Every finding cites one exact transcript event and one exact contract clause, and a generated eval case is kept only if it is run and observed to fail against the skill as it exists today.

## Why install this

Asking a model "how did that run go?" produces a review that sounds right. It
grades from a summary — the user's account, or its own memory of what it just
did — and a summary is exactly where the failures have already been edited out.

eval grades from the transcript instead. It extracts every clause the skill
actually committed to in its own `SKILL.md`, normalizes the session into anchored
events, and keeps only the findings it can cite on both sides: this event, that
clause. A finding whose citation does not resolve is **dropped, not softened** —
a review that hedges is a review nobody acts on.

Then it closes the loop. A confirmed failure that will recur becomes a permanent
eval case, and the case is kept only after it has been run and observed to fail
against the skill as it exists today. A generated test that passes on arrival is
not a regression test; it is a decoration.

## What you get

| Path | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `skills/eval/SKILL.md` | The flow, the one rule, and what may never be graded from. |
| `skills/eval/scripts/eval.js` | The CLI: `contract`, `trace`, `probe`, `report`, `case`. |
| `skills/eval/scripts/lib/` | Clause extraction, trace normalization, the probe catalogue, scoring. |
| `skills/eval/references/rubric.md` | Where a clause comes from, which files are contract versus commentary, and the recall limit that makes the coverage gap load-bearing. |
| `skills/eval/references/probes.md` | The eight probes: what each one decides, and what it explicitly cannot and must hand to judgment. |
| `skills/eval/references/cases.md` | What makes a generated eval case worth keeping. |
| `skills/eval/evals/baseline/` | A real graded run — this repo's own skillfactory session — frozen and re-scored. |

## Quick start

```bash
eval contract --skill skillfactory --out contract.json   # every clause it committed to
eval trace --run session.jsonl --out trace.json   # the run, as citable events
eval probe --contract contract.json --trace trace.json
eval report --contract contract.json --trace trace.json --out ./report
eval case --skill skillfactory --in SKILL.md --assert-absent "<the defect text>" --prove
```

Install from the [claude-skills marketplace](https://github.com/natejswenson/claude-skills),
then point it at a run.

## Triggers

- "evaluate this run"
- "grade this skill"
- "eval this run"
- "how good was that run"
- "did the skill follow its own rules"
- "audit this transcript"
- "write evals for my skill"
- "deepen the evals"
- "my evals are decorative"
- A session transcript that should be checked for results it claimed but never
  observed.

## Requirements

- Node 18+, no dependencies.
- A skill with a committed `SKILL.md` — the contract is read from the skill's own
  file, never supplied separately, so there is nothing to keep in sync.
- A session transcript to grade. Everything is offline: eval never calls a model
  and cannot spend.

## What is code and what is judgment

The split is declared in `skill-invariants.json` and checked — a deterministic
step whose command does not exist fails `skillfactory verify`.

| Deterministic — the machine decides | Command |
|---|---|
| extract every committed clause with a stable id and a source anchor | `eval contract --skill <name>` |
| normalize a session transcript into anchored, citable events | `eval trace --run <file>` |
| decide the mechanically checkable violations and resolve every citation | `eval probe` |
| assemble the scored report and the clause-coverage gap | `eval report` |
| prove a generated eval case fails against the skill as it exists today | `eval case --prove` |

| Model judgment — nothing on disk answers it | Why |
|---|---|
| whether a clause no probe can parse was violated in spirit | the probe catalogue is finite; the contract is prose |
| how to rank findings by what they would actually have cost | severity is about consequence, not about rule count |
| which confirmed findings deserve to become permanent eval cases | a case is maintenance forever, and most findings are not worth it |
| the report prose and the recommended fix for each finding | a fix is a design decision, not a diff |

## Development

```bash
cd skills/eval/skills/eval
npm test
```

Node skill. `ci / eval` runs the same tests plus the house lints on every pull
request, and `skillfactory verify --skill eval` reports which rung of the ladder it has
reached.

The baseline is pinned against a real graded run — this repo's own skillfactory session,
frozen as a normalized trace and scored against skillfactory's frozen contract — plus
every shipped skill's contract as a corpus. It catches the probe catalogue
silently ceasing to fire, clause extraction dropping a rule form so the report
shrinks while still looking complete, `case` accepting an eval that passes on
arrival, and a contract resolver matching nothing and grading an empty rubric as
clean.
